title: gh-ship Configuration
description: Configuration for gh-ship, the GitHub Release Orchestrator. Lives at .github/ship.yml. Only `version` and `workflows.prepare` are required — everything else has a sensible default.

release_branch.description: Branch on which the release is staged. gh-ship creates it if missing and moves it onto each new release commit, so it is machine-managed: anything else pushed there is discarded. Your prepare workflow commits to a throwaway ship/prepare-* branch, which gh-ship then promotes onto this one. This is a MiniJinja template rendered once per release line, with {{ branch }} (the base branch) and {{ match }} (what a `*` in the matching `branches` entry captured, or the branch itself for an exact entry) in context. A `branches` entry may override it. Two release lines must never resolve to the same branch — they would share a Release PR and overwrite each other — so a glob's release branch must vary with what it matches.

branches.description: The base branches gh-ship releases from, one release line each, so a project can maintain release/1.x while main moves on. An entry is either a branch name — a glob if it contains a single `*` — or a mapping with `branch` and its own `release_branch` template, for a line that deviates from the top-level one. Exact entries are matched before globs, and globs in the order listed. When omitted, the repository's own default branch is the only release line. gh-ship detects which branch it runs on from --base, the GitHub Actions environment, the local checkout, or the repository's default branch, in that order. Note that `uniqueItems` cannot see `main` and `{branch: main}` as the same line; gh-ship rejects that itself.

anyOf.title: Branch with its own release branch

branch.description: The base branch this line releases from. A glob if it contains a single `*`.

release_branch.description: This line's release branch template, overriding the top-level one. Same context: {{ branch }} and {{ match }}.

workflows.description: The workflows gh-ship dispatches. These must declare `on: workflow_dispatch` — a `workflow_call`-only (so-called reusable) workflow cannot be started through the API at all. They are referenced by filename slug, so `prepare-release` means `.github/workflows/prepare-release.yaml`.

prepare.description: Workflow that bumps the version, writes the changelog, commits, pushes, and uploads `ship.release.json`.

publish.description: Optional workflow run after the Release PR is merged and the draft release exists — typically builds and uploads assets.

pull_request.description: Release PR rendering. Templates are MiniJinja, with the release artifact as the root context: {{ version }}, {{ tag }}, {{ release.notes }}.

title.description: Template for the PR title. This is also the commit message: GitHub pre-fills the squash-merge dialog from the PR title and appends `(#42)`, so a Conventional Commit here keeps the release commit parseable by changelog tooling.

header.description: Markdown prepended to the release notes.

footer.description: Markdown appended after the release notes.

labels.description: Labels applied to the Release PR. gh-ship creates any that do not exist; if it cannot, it warns and opens the PR without them.

reuse.description: Reuse the existing Release PR instead of opening a new one on every prepare. A closed but unmerged PR is reopened; a merged one is left alone and a new PR is opened. Set to false to close any open Release PR and open a fresh one each time.

draft.description: Create the release as a draft, then publish it once the publish workflow succeeds. This is the default because it is the only ordering that lets the publish workflow attach assets before anyone watching the repository is notified.

pull_request.title: chore(release): {{ version }}
pull_request.header: This PR prepares the next release.
